what: The runtime built four ways and measured in the browser: the physics sample packed with each runtime (`pocket pack physics --web --config <config>`), served by tools/scripts/web_evidence.py, and driven through window.pocket. `step600_ms` is the wall time of `pocket.command('step', {ticks: 600})`, three or four runs in a row (the first includes warm-up); `capture_ms` is one `commandAsync('capture')` (a GPU readback that yields to the event loop). Sizes are pocket_runtime.wasm as packed. The -Oz builds were made once for this comparison and are not configurations of pocket.toml.
browser: Chromium 152 (the Claude desktop app's built-in browser, macOS); WebAssembly.Suspending is defined, so JSPI is available
toolchain: Emscripten 6.0.9, SDL3 and emdawnwebgpu ports; the engine at the commit that adds the wasm-jspi configuration

variants.kept: the default: runs in every browser with WebGPU
a configuration: 31% smaller at the same speed, for browsers with JSPI
not kept: 16% smaller but the simulation runs about 35% slower
not kept: 19% smaller than wasm-jspi but about 18% slower

hello.note: the hello sample under both kept runtimes, for the startup path (adapter and device requests, the IndexedDB mount, all awaited from main) and a capture
